rows.notes: The study is a global meta-analysis of 74 published papers (591 side-by-side comparisons) on deficit versus full irrigation of cotton; it reports no primary data of its own, so Q1 is 'no' and Q2-Q9 follow. For the record, the meta-analysis reports (Section 3.4, Fig. 6a-b) that soil texture did not significantly affect the yield reduction or WP gain under deficit irrigation, and the Discussion (4.4) attributes the texture pattern to poor aeration in fine soils and poor water/nutrient holding in coarse soils by citing other work (Bollmann and Conrad, Tiedje, Du et al.), not by measuring aeration. It does not compare surface and subsurface drip at all; the subsurface-versus-surface drip yield gap in the passage is not examined.

Meta-analysis, not a primary study, so Q1 is 'no'. For the record, the meta-analysis finds (Section 3.2, Fig. 3a-b) that under deficit irrigation the seed cotton yield reduction was similar under drip (-19.5%) and furrow (-19.6%) and largest under sprinkler (-36.2%), with no significant WP difference among methods. The soil-aeration mechanism in the passage appears in the Discussion (4.2) only as an explanation citing Bonachela et al. (2001) and Kang et al. (2004); it was not measured. Nitrogen use efficiency and crop quality are not analysed.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). The study is a meta-analysis of published deficit-irrigation experiments on cotton and so fails Q1 for both rows; its own aggregated results are summarised in the row notes for context only.
